summary: Iteration 65 — Tested the NEW break tracker + regularization + combined attendance hub. Backend: 13/13 pytest cases pass (break start/end lifecycle, double-start 400, break auto-close on check-out with net-based half_day, regularization CRUD with permission checks, approved reg counts as PAID in payroll). Frontend: office admin desktop break UI (Start→End flip, Check out disabled with hint, work-timer shows 'Worked (net)'+'Break …'), regularization dialog fields, combined tabs (attendance/regularize/leave/payroll), super_admin sees Regularize/Leave/Payroll (no Attendance/check-in tab) and ?tab=leave activates Leave tab, staff bottom nav has Attendance and NO Leave, StaffDashboard staff-action-attendance, mobile hero (Worked Hrs + Lunch Break labels, live clock, Goal 9h ring), and mobile-break-btn toggles dial to 'On Break' disabled and back.

issues: mobile-break-btn sits close to the fixed bottom-nav (button center y≈798 in a 844px viewport, ~46px above the bottom nav). Playwright's force-click hit-tests the elementFromPoint and returned an SVG path from an underlying element on the first attempt. Real-user finger taps still work (verified with a scroll-into-view regular click); consider adding a bit of bottom padding to the mobile hero container to avoid edge overlap on smaller phones.

critical_code_review_comments: attendance.check_out uses `rec.get('status') or 'present'` before overriding with half_day if net<4h. This means a 'late' morning check-in remains 'late' unless net<4h (then it becomes half_day). Correct behavior, but the half_day override discards the 'late' flag — payroll only cares about status categories so it's OK; keep in mind if you ever want to surface 'late-and-half' distinctly.

regularizations decide endpoint: office_admin scope check is (office match) AND (user_role=='staff'). If an office_admin ever needs to approve their own peer office_admin's regularization, they will get 403. Currently intentional (per spec 'office_admin non-staff → 403'), just documenting.

_payroll_rows counts status in ('present','late','weekoff','leave') into `present_days`. That's fine for payroll math (present_eq), but the returned column named `present_days` now includes regularized weekoff/leave days, which double-counts if a viewer also reads `leave_days` (leave_map). Currently `lset` subtracts pset/hset so no double count in totals; still, the JSON field naming may confuse UI. UI uses present/half/paid-leave/absent separately so it renders correctly. Consider renaming or splitting for clarity.
